newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico lira bond to help refinancing - government.
newsitem.headline: Mexico lira bond to help refinancing - government.

text.p: Mexico placed another bond in the Italian lira market on Wednesday to allow the federal government to refinance maturing debt in 1997, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.
The 10-year 500 billion lira issue was widely expected, and was led by Chase Securities and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the Ministry said in a news release.
The issue, worth about $310 millon, pays an annual yield of 9.22 percent, equal to 232 basis points over equivalent U.S. Treasuries.

The Ministry said it placed the issue to, "achieve more favourable costs and terms for refinancing maturing federal government external debt in 1997, which is made up of three placements done in 1995, and which had terms of less than three years at the time they were placed."
The Finance Ministry said the issue will help consolidate Mexico's presence in the Italian lira market and extend its investor base.
It added that the placement will allow it to make "substantial" cost savings compared to what it would have had to pay for other available financing.
Analysts said the lira issue fits in with the government's strategy of going to market early and often this year, and with its plan to place more issues in European currencies.
Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz left for a business trip to Switzerland, France and Germany on Wednesday.
With key mid-term elections planned this July, Mexican borrowers in general are seen taking advantage of what could be the calm before the storm.
In November last year, the UMS placed a five-year lira issue, worth about $325 million, at 249 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
In April last year, state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) placed a two-year 300 billion lira bond at 300 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.

The UMS has $1.4 billion in maturing debt this year, but various state agencies, such as Federal Electricity Commission and Pemex, also have issues coming due this year, bringing the market total to $4.047 billion.
